subject: FATAL atom does not have a type crispr cas9 pdb

messages.author: Jisha B
messages.body:
Dear all, I have been trying to generate a topology and parameter file for a CRISPR cas9 system. I have done the pdb4amber -i cas1.pdb -o cas.pdb --reduce --dry In tleap source leaprc.protein.ff14SB source leaprc.RNA.OL3 source leaprc.DNA.bsc1 source leaprc.water.tip3p system = loadpdb cas.pdb addions system Na+ 0 solvatebox system TIP3PBOX 12.0 saveamberparm system cas.prmtop cas.inpcrd But I get the following error. FATAL: Atom .R.A

does not have a type. FATAL: Atom .R.A does not have a type. FATAL: Atom .R.A does not have a type. How to solve this problem? Kindly advise -- Jisha

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Sun, Aug 30, 2020, Jisha B wrote: >FATAL: Atom .R.A

does not have a type. FATAL: Atom .R1523>.A does not have a type. FATAL: Atom .R.A >does not have a type. Amber's standard 5' terminal DNA residues do not have a phosphate group. If *all* your 5' DNA's have a dangling phosphate, then try loading terminal_monophosphate.lib after sourcing leaprc.DNA.OL15. (Take a look at the terminal_monophosphate.lib library to see what it is doing.) An alternative is to use the method described in Section 3.2.3 of the Amber20 Reference Manual. ...hope this helps....dac
